2
Which combination of units could be used for expressing the power dissipated in a resistor?
A
newton per second (N s–1)
B
newton second (N s)
C
newton metre (N m)
D
newton metre per second (N m s–1)

hints: Notice the question asks for power dissipated, which means energy transferred per unit time with SI unit watt.
Recall that work done is force times distance, so $1 \text{ N}$ times $1 \text{ m}$ equals $1 \text{ J}$ of energy.
Check which of the four newton combinations first makes a joule and then divides that energy by seconds to make joules per second.
walkthrough: Identify what is needed: power $P$ is the rate of energy transfer, $P = W/t$, with unit joule per second or watt.
Recall the mechanical definition of work: work $W = F \times d$, so one joule is one newton metre, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$.
Combine the two ideas: power unit $= \text{energy unit} / \text{time unit} = \text{J s}^{-1} = \text{N m s}^{-1}$.
Compare with the options: newton per second and newton second involve force divided or multiplied by time, and newton metre alone is only energy.
Therefore only newton metre per second matches joules per second. This is option D.

A.explanation: A newton divided by second, $\text{N s}^{-1}$, is force per time and does not give energy per time.

B.explanation: A newton times second, $\text{N s}$, is force times time, the unit of impulse and momentum, not power.

C.explanation: A newton times metre, $\text{N m}$, equals the joule, the unit of work and energy dissipated, not the rate of dissipation.

D.explanation: A newton metre is work and dividing by second gives work per time, which is power in watts.
